lessons: Use check_after on promising alternatives, especially when few candidates are feasible or some offered stones are unplaceable. Favor preserving next poses for many other offered stones, particularly constrained ones. A zero is a warning, not permanent loss: later placements may reopen poses, and unoffered stones are not checked.

When a large or awkward offered stone has few feasible poses, consider placing it rather than saving it indefinitely. Check whether alternatives would leave it without a next pose. Do not assume that rotating it upright will solve the problem.

Among choices that preserve placement options, favor higher LLC, particularly when alternatives differ sharply. Avoid giving up much LLC merely to maximize another score. LLC is a useful stability proxy, not a guarantee of the finished wall’s limit load.

Do not maximize course-level NHR or interlocking IWR in isolation. Balance joint staggering with stability and fit; accept some height mismatch when it preserves good alternatives. An exceptionally high IWR can accompany a poor or incomplete wall.

For otherwise comparable candidates, favor higher GDS and LFR closer to zero. But a locally dense, flush placement can still leave a poor or incomplete wall, so do not put either score ahead of preserving stones and maintaining stability.
